intro.bio:
Couple decades behind the turntables. Scratching with rap groups and DJs of all kinds, mixing all sorts of styles in trendy bars, fashionable buvettes and at special events across Quebec.

I've also been DJ Muhammad Alias and DJ Alias in the past.

reviews.simone.text: Groove placed at just the right moments thanks to his keen ear for the atmosphere. Always on the lookout to share little musical gems with us.
reviews.tmo.text: A great guy, with a unique sense of humour, and a formidable DJ, capable of being technically skilled, but also of animating the crowd and making the right musical choices.
reviews.jessie.text: We hired him for our opening at Le Birdie and he delivered top-notch. Perfect atmosphere, great personality. A true pro!

school.method.history.title: history
school.method.history.intro: take a look at where it all started|how it evolved|who are the pillars|what are tools|how to stand out
school.method.history.early-beginnings.b: We'll take a quick look at what is the base principles of being a DJ. What it means. Who did it first and who followed.
school.method.history.the-evolution.body: Who brought the innovation? Smoother transitions, the scratch, the beat juggle and all the new effects and fresh tricks coming from the new generation of tech.
school.method.history.the-big-pillars.bo: Some DJs became legends. They added key elements to the art and brought them to our ears and eyes.
school.method.history.the-tools.title: the tools
school.method.history.the-tools.body: From turntables to controllers, a lot of gear was designed and used trough the last decades. Most of them created new paths to explore.
school.method.history.be-unique.title: be unique
school.method.history.be-unique.body: Find what can make you stand out and be different than the other DJs.

school.method.mix.listen-to-music.title: listen to music
school.method.mix.listen-to-music.body: There is a lot of music out there. There is also a lot of DJs out there too now. To define your signature you need to dig. Listen to a LOT of music and find what fits with you and your style.
school.method.mix.the-right-tracks.title: the right tracks
school.method.mix.the-right-tracks.body: People like to hear what they know and like most of the time. But some like to hear stuff they don't know about. Shazam something that will make them go “wow! did not know about that!”
school.method.mix.set-the-mood.title: set the mood
school.method.mix.set-the-mood.body: You should not play the same sets at all events you get to play at. Sure, define your style and play it. But allow yourself to improvise, read the room and explore. Then, people who see you twice or more do not think you’re just a playlist.
school.method.mix.beat-match.title: beat match
school.method.mix.beat-match.body: Great transitions need to be smoother than butter. Set the right BPM to match the songs together. Select a song in an exact or similar key so they hold hands while they move together.
school.method.mix.build-your-sets.title: build your sets
school.method.mix.build-your-sets.body: Place strategic digital cue points or find and remember where the vinyl sweet spot is so you can begin and end your transitions fashionably.
school.method.scratch.the-techniques.bod: From “baby scratch” to “double click flare” there is a world of chops and sounds to discover. Let’s play around and fine tune the different scratches execution.
school.method.scratch.practice.title: practice
school.method.scratch.practice.body: Fingers and ear coordination is a bit tricky to develop so we’ll practice. I’ll show you how to execute the technique and you’ll go home and practice. Repetition brings perfection.
school.method.scratch.how-and-when.title: how and when
school.method.scratch.how-and-when.body: Scratching is not for everybody and should not be over used all the time. We’ll explore what works best in several DJ situations and how to be ready to execute precise scratches in specific key situations.
school.method.scratch.style.title: style
school.method.scratch.style.body: Babu, Q-Bert and A-Trak are definite GOATS but do not have the same style. We’ll spot what seems to fit you best and develop the scratches that match your style the better.
school.reviews.mathieu.name: Mathieu
school.reviews.mathieu.text: I took DJ lessons with Momo and the experience was really great. He put me at ease and built real trust, which let me learn to scratch and progress fast thanks to the work he gave me between sessions. I even got to mix at a party with him, with all his support. I recommend him to everyone.
school.reviews.roger.name: Roger
school.reviews.roger.text: Generous with his time and his knowledge, he got me started with gear and good advice. And when he performs, live or on stream, his music selection and transitions speak for themselves. A real source of inspiration.
why.title: why
why.intro: goals are productive|people need a hand|science helps a lot|care and inspire
why.goals-are-productive.title: goals are productive
why.goals-are-productive.body: Setting yourself a goal limits the time spent doubting. And since time is precious, we should spend most of it doing good things.
why.people-need-a-hand.title: people need a hand
why.people-need-a-hand.body: I needed a hand this past year. I was lucky to meet the right people at the right time, and to benefit instantly from my family's, friends' and community's support. But not everybody has the same chance, at the right moment or at all. So let's be there for them.
why.science-helps-a-lot.title: science helps a lot
why.science-helps-a-lot.body: To battle cancer, science shows up. It did for me and for all of us battling this beast every day — helping to spot it fast and precisely, to get the cancer out efficiently, and to minimise the aftershock so people can go back to their life in a flash.
why.care-and-inspire.title: care and inspire
why.care-and-inspire.body: Just like the Quebec Cancer Foundation, I'd like you to join the fundraiser to give back to the people who need extra help while facing this challenging situation — providing someone to talk to, shelter, therapy and many other game-changing services to cancer fighters across Quebec.
